ns2:section.sectionText: Collections, documents, texts, stories, sounds, and images are foundational entities in library and information science. It is surprising then that we understand so little about what these things really are. As the world of digital information systems becomes increasingly formal and rigorous this lack of understanding creates problems for the design of systems and services. To prepare us for addressing these problems, this course explores the fundamental nature of the key entities in our field. The method of approach will be conceptual analysis and formal ontology. The course will be conducted as an advanced seminar. Although there are no specific prerequisites, students should be comfortable learning and using formal languages. There will be a tutorial on elementary symbolic logic.
ns2:section.sectionDeptRestriction: Restricted to students in the Library & Information Science department.
